title: Linear Search Check
description: First-match scans, complexity, and missing targets.

questions.prompt: For `arr = [4, 9, 2, 9]` and `target = 9`, classic first-match linear search returns:
questions.explanation: The scan returns the first matching index. Index `1` holds the first `9`.

questions.prompt: Linear search requires the array to be sorted.
questions.explanation: Linear search needs no sorted order — that is why it is the default when binary search is unavailable.

questions.prompt: Worst-case time for linear search of length `n` is:
questions.explanation: Missing target or last element forces up to `n` comparisons → `O(n)`.

questions.prompt: Returning early on the first match means the algorithm is no longer linear search.

options.text: True — early exit makes it binary search
False — early exit is still linear search and is required for first index

questions.explanation: Early return is normal linear search for first-match. Worst case remains `O(n)`.
